dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hi, yeah, good morning. Um, so my name's Bruce Lawton, and I should say up front, I'm bad at phone calls. Always have been. My sister says I talk like I'm writing a book with no chapters.
That's all right, take your time, Bruce. What's going on?

Okay, so. I'm a homeowner, but a few weeks back the tenant who rented the other side of the house moved out. It's a two-family, I own the whole thing, no wait, that's not the point. The point is the old landlord, the guy who had the lease before I bought it, he came back after the move-out and cleaned out the unit. Mattress, a busted dresser, a couple of chairs, all of it piled at the curb.
Okay, so a landlord left bulk waste at the curb after a move-out. Is that right?

Right, right. And I figured, well, it's bulk, somebody'll come get it. Which, I mean, it's been there since, let me think, the Saturday after New Year's. Before that I was at my cousin's for the, no, never mind. So it's been there almost a week.
Alright. And was it set out for a scheduled pickup, or did anyone call it in to have it collected?
That's the thing, I don't think anybody called. He just dropped it and left. I didn't know you had to call. I figured it was like regular trash day.
Okay. Usually bulk items need to be requested ahead of time, they don't get picked up with the regular trash. So nothing's been scheduled that I can see from what you're telling me.

Yeah, that tracks. So how do I request one? A replacement, I guess, a, what do you call it, a new pickup. Because the first one never happened, since it was never set up. You know what I mean? I'm doing it again, I'm rambling.
No, I follow you. You want to request a bulk pickup for those items. I can take that request here. I'll need the address where the items are sitting. Can you give me that?
Oh, um, actually, can I hold off on that? I'm not at the house right now, I'm at work, and I don't want to read it wrong. Can I just ask what you need and call back?
Sure. I'd need the street address, what the items are, so the mattress, dresser, chairs, and a phone number to reach you. Just so crews know what to bring.
Okay, mattress, dresser, two chairs. Wait, was it two or three chairs? I'll count when I get home. Anyway, my number's 401-555-0171, if you need it on file.
Got it, 401-555-0171. And I'll note that you're Bruce Lawton, and you're calling about bulk items left after a move-out. When you call back, just mention that and we'll pick it up from there.
Perfect. And do I need to move it, like, off the sidewalk or anything?
Best to keep it at the curb and out of the walkway, so it's easy for the crew to see and nobody trips over it.
Okay. That's easy. It's already right where it was dumped. Alright, thanks, Lorraine. Sorry about the long way around.
You're fine, Bruce. Call back with that address and we'll get the request in. Have a good day.
You too. Bye.
